  [[ "$label" == number-onboarding ]] || resource_conflicts+=("volume:$name")
done < <(docker.exe volume ls --format '{{.Name}}')
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [[ "$name" == "$PROJECT"_* ]] || continue
  label="$(docker.exe network inspect -f '{{ index .Labels "com.leadshug.channels.owner" }}' "$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [[ "$label" == number-onboarding ]] || resource_conflicts+=("network:$name")
done < <(docker.exe network ls --format '{{.Name}}')
if ((${#resource_conflicts[@]})); then
  echo 'Refusing to adopt colliding operator namespace resources without the expected owner label.' >&2
  printf '%s\n' "${resource_conflicts[@]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

case "$ACTION" in
  init) ;;
  config) ;;
  up)
    # Only inspect the intended port immediately before startup; never stop or
    # reconfigure another listener to make room.
    owned_gateway=0
    mapfile -t published_containers < <(docker.exe ps --filter "publish=$HOST_PORT" --format '{{.Names}}')
    for name in "${published_containers[@]}"; do
      if [[ "$name" == "$PROJECT-gateway-"* ]] && [[ "$(docker.exe inspect -f '{{ index .Config.Labels "com.leadshug.channels.owner" }}' "$name")" == number-onboarding ]]; then
        owned_gateway=1
      else
        echo "Host port $HOST_PORT is already published by another container: $name" >&2; exit 1
      fi
    done
    if [[ "$owned_gateway" == 0 ]]; then
      if ! command -v powershell.exe >/dev/null || ! powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "if (Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen -LocalPort $HOST_PORT -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { exit 42 }" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Host port $HOST_PORT is occupied by a process; choose a free CHANNELS_GATEWAY_HOST_PORT." >&2; exit 1
      fi
    fi
    "${compose[@]}" up -d postgres evolution-postgres evolution-redis
    "${compose[@]}" build api
    "${compose[@]}" run --rm api npx prisma migrate deploy
    "${compose[@]}" up -d --build
    "${compose[@]}" ps
    ;;
  bootstrap)
    command -v flock >/dev/null || { echo 'flock is required to serialize the one-shot OWNER bootstrap.' >&2; exit 1; }
    exec {bootstrap_lock_fd}>/tmp/leadshug-channels-local-bootstrap.lock
    flock -n "$bootstrap_lock_fd" || { echo 'Another OWNER bootstrap is in progress.' >&2; exit 1; }
    owner_name=''
    owner_email=''
    owner_password=''
    bootstrap_status=''
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      case "$line" in
        CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_NAME=*) owner_name="${line#*=}" ;;
        CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_EMAIL=*) owner_email="${line#*=}" ;;
        CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER_PASSWORD=*) owner_password="${line#*=}" ;;
        CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS=*) bootstrap_status="${line#*=}" ;;
      esac
    done < "$ENV_FILE"
    [[ -n "$owner_name" && -n "$owner_email" && -n "$owner_password" ]] || { echo 'Private OWNER bootstrap fields are missing.' >&2; exit 1; }
    [[ "$bootstrap_status" == not-started ]] || { echo "OWNER bootstrap status is '$bootstrap_status'; refusing another POST." >&2; exit 1; }
    sed -i 's/^CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS=not-started$/CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS=in-flight/' "$ENV_FILE"
    if printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$owner_name" "$owner_email" "$owner_password" | "${compose[@]}" exec -T api node -e '
let raw = "";
process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
process.stdin.on("data", (chunk) => { raw += chunk; });
process.stdin.on("end", async () => {
  const [ownerName, ownerEmail, ownerPassword] = raw.split("\n");
  try {
    const response = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/internal/mantenedoras", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "x-internal-token": process.env.INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN },
      body: JSON.stringify({ nome: "LeadsHug local test", bu: { nome: "Local Test BU" }, owner: { nome: ownerName, email: ownerEmail, senha: ownerPassword } }),
    });
    let data;
    try { data = await response.json(); } catch {}
    const ids = { mantenedoraId: data?.mantenedora?.id, businessUnitId: data?.businessUnit?.id, ownerId: data?.owner?.id };
    const success = response.status === 201 && Object.values(ids).every(Boolean);
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ httpStatus: response.status, success, ...(success ? ids : {}) }));
    if (!success) process.exitCode = 1;
  } catch {
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ success: false, error: "request_failed" }));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
});
'; then
      sed -i 's/^CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS=in-flight$/CHANNELS_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS=complete/' "$ENV_FILE"
# This file is included from nginx's http context. Deliberately omit request
# target, query, headers and body from every gateway log.
log_format leadshug_safe '$time_iso8601 method=$request_method status=$status bytes=$bytes_sent request_time=$request_time upstream_status=$upstream_status upstream_time=$upstream_response_time';
# Disable the base nginx image's inherited main format, which includes $request.
# The server below installs the redacted access format explicitly.
access_log off;
error_log /dev/null emerg;
map $http_x_forwarded_proto $leadshug_forwarded_proto {
    "~^(https?)$" $http_x_forwarded_proto;
    default $scheme;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;
    access_log /dev/stdout leadshug_safe;
    # API upload ceiling is 1 MiB; leave room for multipart framing.
    client_max_body_size 2m;

    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $leadshug_forwarded_proto;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
    proxy_connect_timeout 10s;
    proxy_send_timeout 120s;
    proxy_read_timeout 120s;

    location = /health {
        proxy_pass http://api:3000;
    }

    location = /ws {
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_read_timeout 1h;
        proxy_pass http://api:3000;
    }

    location = /api {
        proxy_pass http://api:3000;
    }

    location ^~ /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://api:3000;
    }

    location ^~ /webhooks/ {
        proxy_pass http://api:3000;
    }

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://web:80;
    }
}

# LeadsHug runtime workspace

This repository composes the current LeadsHug API, Web application, and the
isolated local channel integration runtime. Product authority lives in
`foundation_documentation`; implementation lives in the API and Web
submodules.

## Components

| Path | Role | Technology |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api-app` | API and domain services | NestJS, Prisma, PostgreSQL |
| `web-app` | Browser application | React, Vite, Nginx |
| `docker-compose.channels.yml` | Isolated operator and validation overlays | Compose, Nginx, Evolution API |
| `foundation_documentation` | Product decisions, TODOs, and contracts | LeadsHug Foundation |
| `delphi-ai` | Local engineering rules and tools | PACED / Delphi |

## Generic local startup

Initialize submodules and create the root local configuration:

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
cp .env.example .env
# Generate values for SESSION_SECRET and INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN.
```

Set `SESSION_SECRET` and `INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN` in `.env`; do not commit it.
The generic stack does not require a global WhatsApp token. Start the default
stack with `make up`, check `http://localhost:3000/health`, and open the Web
application at `http://localhost:8080`. The local PostgreSQL endpoint is
`localhost:55433`.

## Continuous integration

The root workflow validates Compose and runs the API and Web suites
independently. Because those repositories are private submodules, configure
the GitHub Actions secret `SUBMODULES_REPO_TOKEN` with read access to both
repositories before merging a pull request.

## Channel runtime

The operator stack uses a separate Compose project and database from the
disposable browser-validation stack. It publishes only the gateway on loopback;
API, PostgreSQL, Evolution, and Redis stay on the private Compose network.

```bash
make channels-init
make channels-up
make channels-bootstrap
make channels-ps
```

`channels-init` creates ignored `.env.testing` only when that file is absent.
It generates local secrets and one test OWNER credential set there without
displaying values; read the file locally to obtain the login. `channels-bootstrap`
creates the Mantenedora, BU, and OWNER through the authenticated internal
product endpoint. It issues one POST and refuses to retry an ambiguous result.
No email is sent. The disposable browser-validation stack uses a separate DB
and network, and its fixtures are never routed through the operator gateway.

The gateway listens on `http://localhost:8083` by default. Startup-script
defaults take precedence over values in `.env.testing`; pass port, browser
origin, and runtime mode in the command environment when overriding them:

```bash
CHANNELS_GATEWAY_HOST_PORT=8084 \
CHANNELS_LOCAL_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8084 \
CHANNELS_NODE_ENV=development make channels-up
```

`CHANNELS_NODE_ENV=production` enables Secure cookies, so the browser must use
HTTPS. The owned Evolution callback can use the private Compose URL
`http://api:3000/webhooks/evolution`; it does not need a public HTTPS hostname.
Meta's public callback and SDK flows do require a verified HTTPS origin. Keep
the Meta credential group blank until all required fields are available, and
leave unofficial pairing disabled until the pinned Evolution image's header
and log probes pass. Never expose validation fixtures or seed services through
the operator gateway or a tunnel. `make channels-stop` stops only the owned
operator project and preserves its database and files.

## Validation

Run one isolated target at a time:

```bash
make test-channels-api
make test-channels-web
make test-channels-browser
# or all three
make test-channels
```

The runner uses Node 22 and PostgreSQL 16, checks OpenSSL 3 and the source bind
before installing dependencies, masks the API dotenv file inside the
container, and uses only fixture credentials and the disposable
`leadshug_timeline_channels_ci` database. Browser fixtures and seed endpoints
remain internal to this validation project and are never routed through the
operator gateway.

The existing generic Compose targets (`make up`, `down`, `ps`, `logs`,
`test-api`, `test-web`, and `migrate`) remain available for the workspace's
default stack. The `channels-*` and `test-channels*` targets use the separate,
explicitly owned channel namespaces.

## Delphi

The first checkout needs Delphi configured locally:

```bash
bash delphi-ai/init.sh
bash delphi-ai/verify_context.sh --repair
bash delphi-ai/verify_context.sh
```

The Foundation constitution is the project-specific authority. Do not infer a
runtime target, database, tenant policy, or deployment configuration merely
from the presence of a Delphi capability.
